explanation: Horses had died out in the Americas thousands of years earlier. Once nations such as the Comanche and Lakota took them up, they could hunt bison and travel far faster.

claims.text: Horses introduced by the Spanish transformed hunting, travel and warfare among the peoples of the Great Plains.
Bison and llamas are native to the Americas, and donkeys did not transform life on the Plains as horses did.
Native horses died out in the Americas thousands of years before Europeans arrived.
Plains nations such as the Comanche and Lakota became horse-riding peoples who hunted bison on horseback.

Bison and llamas are native to the Americas, and donkeys never transformed Plains life.
The native horses of the Americas died out roughly 10,000 years ago, at the end of the last ice age.

evidence.restatement: The Comanche, Lakota and other Plains nations became mounted bison hunters.
Horses, brought by the Spanish and spread north by trade and raiding, transformed hunting, travel and warfare on the Great Plains.

claimResults.note: Rival test: the donkey and mule also came with the Spanish but did not remake Plains life; bison and llamas were already American.

evidence.restatement: Bison and llamas are native to the Americas; donkeys came from Spain but did not change Plains life as horses did.
Native American horses went extinct about 10,000 years ago, long before European contact.
The Comanche and Lakota became mounted bison hunters.
